Description: Stable deterministic film identifier inherited unchanged from Canonical Film Catalogue v2.1.
Allowed values: Unique non-null value; examples: WDAS_2013_FROZEN, DWA_2001_SHREK
Missing policy: Never missing.
Analytical use: Join key across catalogue, financial, rating, and derived data.

Description: Canonical English film title inherited from the approved catalogue.
Missing policy: Never missing.
Analytical use: Labels, tooltips, source matching, auditability.

Description: Producing studio used for the approved analytical attribution.
Allowed values: Walt Disney Animation Studios; Pixar Animation Studios; DreamWorks Animation; Walt Disney Pictures
Missing policy: Never missing.
Analytical use: Studio-specific comparisons and release-frequency aggregation while preserving Pixar as a distinct studio.

Description: High-level analytical layer frozen in Canonical Film Catalogue v2.1.
Missing policy: Never missing for included films.
Transformation / derivation: Task 4 uses only Task 2 v2.1 rows with inclusion_status == INCLUDE.
Analytical use: Separates WDAS/DreamWorks core films, the Disney-side Pixar layer, and the separate Disney remake/reimagining layer.

Description: Specific frozen corpus assignment from Canonical Film Catalogue v2.1.
Missing policy: Never missing for included films.
Analytical use: Exact layer filtering without inferring analytical membership from studio or corporate ownership.

Description: Deterministic two-side analytical grouping for the revised Disney-vs-DreamWorks framing. Pixar remains a separate studio but belongs to the Disney side.
Source: Derived deterministically from Canonical Film Catalogue v2.1 corpus_assignment
Missing policy: Never missing for included films.
Transformation / derivation: Disney if corpus_assignment in {CORE_WDAS, DISNEY_PIXAR, DISNEY_REMAKE}; DreamWorks if corpus_assignment == CORE_DWA.
Analytical use: Supports two-side Disney-vs-DreamWorks aggregation. Remake rows must still be filtered explicitly with corpus_role/corpus_assignment when computing animated/core comparisons.

Description: Corporate parent/group associated with the producing studio at the film's release date.
Allowed values: Controlled company/group names as frozen in Task 2
Fallback source: Official corporate history / acquisition sources already used in Task 2
Missing policy: Missing only if Task 2 did not assign a corporate group.
Analytical use: Distinguishes pre-acquisition Pixar partnership releases from post-acquisition Disney ownership and preserves DreamWorks ownership history without changing studio identity.

Description: Canonical release date frozen in Task 2 and used as the project time coordinate.
Fallback source: None; external release data are cross-checks only
Missing policy: Never missing for included films.
Transformation / derivation: Do not overwrite with TMDB or The Numbers dates.
Analytical use: Timeline, release frequency, temporal trends, CPI month matching.

Description: Calendar year of the canonical release date.
Missing policy: Never missing for included films.
Transformation / derivation: year(release_date); Task 2 value is preserved and validated.
Analytical use: Annual release counts and temporal aggregation.

Description: Whether the target studio is the sole credited producer or a co-producer.
Missing policy: Never missing for included films.
Analytical use: Production attribution audit and co-production sensitivity checks.

Description: Other formally credited production partners recorded for a co-production.
Allowed values: Free text company names; blank for sole productions
Fallback source: Official film credits / authoritative industry record
Missing policy: Blank is expected for sole_production; should be populated for co_production when identifiable.
Analytical use: Traceability and verification of studio attribution; not a primary performance metric.

Description: Approved initial distribution model relevant to theatrical eligibility.
Fallback source: Task 2 v2.1 release evidence; TMDB release_dates endpoint for cross-check only
Missing policy: Never missing for included films.
Analytical use: Separates standard theatrical performance from limited or simultaneous streaming cases.

Description: Context flag for release conditions that materially affect comparability.
Missing policy: Never missing for included films.
Analytical use: Sensitivity analysis and annotation of COVID-era or otherwise exceptional releases.

Description: Form classification needed to distinguish animated competitor/core films from Disney live-action or photorealistic remake context.
Missing policy: Never missing for included films.
Analytical use: Prevents inappropriate direct comparisons between animated core titles and Disney remake-context forms.

Description: Film's relationship to an existing screen property under Dataset Scope v2.0.
Missing policy: Never missing for included films.
Analytical use: Comparison of first entries and franchise extensions over time.

Description: Canonical umbrella screen-franchise label, when the film belongs to a franchise as of the frozen cutoff.
Allowed values: Canonical franchise name; blank for films with no identified franchise membership
Source: Official studio/franchise sources consistent with Canonical Film Catalogue v2.1
Fallback source: The Numbers franchise metadata / authoritative trade source
Missing policy: Blank for non-franchise films; must be non-blank for sequel, prequel, spin_off, or remake_reimagining unless the property has no meaningful umbrella label.
Transformation / derivation: No automated inference from title strings.
Analytical use: Groups franchise entries and supports franchise concentration / recurrence views.

Description: Observable source-basis classification, kept distinct from franchise status.
Missing policy: Never missing for included films.
Analytical use: Separates new screen IP from adaptations and existing screen properties without inventing an originality score.

Description: TMDB movie identifier used for reproducible API retrieval of audience fields.
Fallback source: None; resolve ambiguous matches manually using title/year/studio evidence
Missing policy: Missing only if no reliable TMDB match exists; do not substitute a different rating platform.
Transformation / derivation: Matched using canonical title/year and verified before retrieval.
Analytical use: Stable key for rating snapshots and API reproducibility.

Description: Exact film-level financial source page used for budget and box-office extraction.
Allowed values: Usually a The Numbers film page; fallback source URL when primary data are unavailable
Fallback source: Box Office Mojo for grosses; official/trade source for budget
Missing policy: Required whenever any financial field is populated.
Analytical use: Row-level traceability of commercial data.

Description: Single production-budget value reported by the selected source, in contemporaneous nominal U.S. dollars.
Allowed values: >= 0; zero is not accepted as a missing-data placeholder
Fallback source: Official studio/corporate disclosure or reputable trade reporting
Missing policy: NA when unavailable or when only an unresolved range exists. Never impute. Source 0/n/a placeholders are converted to NA.
Transformation / derivation: Currency normalization to USD only when the source explicitly reports USD; do not infer exchange rates silently.
Analytical use: Budget scale, gross-to-budget descriptive ratio, commercial-data quality assessment.

Description: Lower bound when the best credible budget evidence is a reported range.
Missing policy: NA unless a credible range is explicitly reported.
Transformation / derivation: Do not create a range from informal disagreement between weak sources.
Analytical use: Preserves uncertainty rather than collapsing ranges to arbitrary midpoints.

Description: Upper bound when the best credible budget evidence is a reported range.
Missing policy: NA unless a credible range is explicitly reported.
Transformation / derivation: Do not replace a range with its midpoint.
Analytical use: Budget uncertainty and data-quality reporting.

Description: Quality/type flag describing how the stored production budget should be interpreted.
Missing policy: Never missing.
Transformation / derivation: Classified after source review; does not imply audited accounting precision.
Analytical use: Data-quality assessment and filtering/sensitivity checks.

Description: Concise note for material budget ambiguity, source conflict, or range interpretation.
Missing policy: Blank when no non-trivial issue exists.
Analytical use: Traceability for known budget-quality issues.

Description: Cumulative domestic theatrical box-office gross reported by the financial source.
Missing policy: NA if unavailable. Never infer from worldwide gross.
Transformation / derivation: Use the source's cumulative domestic theatrical total as retrieved.
Analytical use: Primary long-run commercial comparison after CPI normalization; nominal value retained for audit.

Description: Cumulative international theatrical box-office gross reported by the financial source.
Fallback source: Box Office Mojo when explicitly available
Missing policy: NA if unavailable; do not derive silently as worldwide minus domestic.
Analytical use: Commercial-data reconciliation and optional domestic/international context.

Description: Cumulative worldwide theatrical box-office gross reported by the financial source.
Missing policy: NA if unavailable. Never impute from budget, rating, or other performance variables.
Transformation / derivation: Use source-reported worldwide total rather than reconstructing when available.
Analytical use: Worldwide commercial scale and gross-to-budget descriptive ratio.

Description: Concise note for non-trivial box-office source issues or incomplete/current theatrical runs.
Missing policy: Blank when no non-trivial issue exists.
Analytical use: Data-quality interpretation, especially recent or anomalously distributed films.

Description: TMDB movie vote_average captured as a dated snapshot.
Fallback source: None; do not mix rating platforms
Missing policy: If tmdb_vote_count == 0, store rating as NA rather than interpreting API zero as a real audience score.
Analytical use: Audience reception comparison by studio, period, corpus, and franchise status.

Description: Number of TMDB votes underlying the captured user rating.
Missing policy: NA only if the TMDB record cannot be retrieved; 0 is a valid count.
Analytical use: Rating reliability/context and sensitivity analysis; not treated as a pure popularity measure.

Description: Date on which financial values were retrieved.
Missing policy: Required whenever any financial field is populated.
Analytical use: Reproducibility because current/recent box-office totals can change.

Description: Date on which TMDB vote_average and vote_count were captured.
Missing policy: Required whenever TMDB audience fields are populated.
Analytical use: Makes time-varying audience metrics reproducible as a snapshot.

Description: Binary analytical grouping separating first screen entries from extensions of existing screen properties.
Missing policy: Never missing when franchise_status is present.
Transformation / derivation: TRUE if franchise_status in {sequel, prequel, spin_off, remake_reimagining}; FALSE if first_entry.
Analytical use: Compares first entries with sequels, prequels, spin-offs, and remakes/reimaginings without creating a subjective originality score.

Description: Domestic theatrical gross converted to July 2026 U.S. consumer-price purchasing power.
Source: Derived from The Numbers domestic gross and BLS CPI-U
Missing policy: NA if domestic gross or the corresponding monthly CPI is missing.
Transformation / derivation: domestic_box_office_usd_nominal * 333.918 / CPI_U(release month), where 333.918 is July 2026 CPI-U, U.S. city average, all items, not seasonally adjusted.
Analytical use: Main inflation-normalized domestic box-office comparison across time.

Description: Worldwide theatrical gross divided by the point production-budget value.
Missing policy: NA if worldwide gross or point budget is missing, if budget <= 0, or if only a budget range is available.
Analytical use: Descriptive comparison of theatrical gross relative to production-budget scale.

Description: Month identifying the CPI observation used for inflation normalization.
Missing policy: No missing months expected in the required interval; any source gap must be documented rather than interpolated silently.
Analytical use: Join key from film release month to CPI-U.

Description: Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers, U.S. city average, All items, not seasonally adjusted.
Missing policy: Do not interpolate silently; document any unavailable source observation.
Analytical use: Inflation normalization of domestic box office.

Description: Human-readable identifier of the CPI series used throughout the project.
Allowed values: CPI-U All items, U.S. city average, not seasonally adjusted (1982-84=100)
Missing policy: Never missing.
Analytical use: Prevents accidental mixing of CPI series.

Description: Date on which the CPI series snapshot was retrieved.
Missing policy: Never missing.
Analytical use: Reproducibility and data-version traceability.
